title: Six weeks, one developer, Claude Code: what the AI did and didn't do on my tactical game
author: dystostorm
selftext:
Silent Entry: a top-down hostage-rescue game in Godot 4, now with a story and a free demo. Some notes on the workflow, for anyone doing the same:

AI did:

almost all the code (\~34k lines of GDScript, \~9k lines of Python tools); the procedural 3D world; retargeting animations onto the character models in Blender; a pixel-art version of the same game; the build, release and marketing scripts (it records the cutscene with Godot's Movie Maker and cuts the clips itself).

I did:

the design, every decision, playing it constantly, and catching what looks wrong. The AI is fast, but it doesn't play your game.



What kept it on the rails:

1. One handoff doc that every session reads first (architecture, numbers, gotchas, roadmap).

2. Automated scenario tests for every mechanic (115 now), run after every change.

3. Screenshots after every visual change, reviewed before moving on.

4. Small steps, committed one at a time, so a bad change is easy to undo.

No AI art or sound: licensed models, CC0 textures, a sound library and scripted effects.

Free demo (Windows/Linux) in the comments. What does your setup look like?
